runs.text: The doctrine of natural immortality has prepared the way for modern Spiritualism. If the dead are admitted to the presence of God and holy angels, and privileged with knowledge far exceeding what they before possessed, why should they not return to the earth to enlighten and instruct the living? How can those who believe in man’s consciousness in death reject what comes to them as divine light communicated by glorified spirits? Here is a channel regarded as sacred, through which Satan works for the accomplishment of his purposes. The fallen angels who do his bidding appear as messengers from the spirit world. While professing to bring the living into communication with the dead, Satan exercises his bewitching influence upon their minds.

He has power even to bring before men the appearance of their departed friends. The counterfeit is perfect; the familiar look, the words, the tone, are reproduced with marvelous distinctness. Many are comforted with the assurance that their loved ones are enjoying the bliss of Heaven; and without suspicion of danger, they give ear to seducing spirits and doctrines of devils.

When they have been led to believe that the dead actually return to communicate with them, Satan causes those to appear who went into the grave unprepared. They claim to be happy in Heaven and even to occupy exalted positions there; thus the error is widely taught that no difference is made between the righteous and the wicked. These pretended visitants sometimes utter cautions and warnings which prove correct. Then, as confidence is gained, they insinuate dangerous errors that directly undermine faith in the Scriptures.

paragraphs.text: The position that it is of no consequence what men believe, is one of Satan’s most successful deceptions. He knows that the truth, received in the love of it, sanctifies the soul of the receiver; therefore he is constantly seeking to substitute false theories, fables, … another gospel.

runs.text: With an appearance of deep interest in the well-being of their friends on earth, they state some truths and foretell future events, giving their statements an appearance of reliability. Their false teachings are accepted as readily as if they were the most sacred truths of the Bible. The law of God is set aside, the Spirit of grace despised, the blood of the covenant counted an unholy thing. The spirits deny the divinity of Christ and place even the Creator on a level with them selves. Thus under a new disguise the great rebel still carries on his warfare against God, begun in Heaven and continued upon the earth for nearly six thousand years.

Many try to account for spiritual manifestations by attributing them wholly to fraud and sleight of hand by the medium. While trickery has often been palmed off as genuine, there have also been marked exhibitions of supernatural power. The mysterious rapping with which modern Spiritualism began was not the result of human trickery, but the direct work of evil angels, introducing one of the most successful soul-destroying delusions. Many will be ensnared through believing Spiritualism is merely human imposture; when confronted with undeniable supernatural manifestations, they will be deceived and accept them as the great power of God.

These persons overlook Scripture’s testimony about the wonders wrought by Satan and his agents. By Satanic aid Pharaoh’s magicians counterfeited God’s work. John describes the miracle-working power in the last days: “He doeth great wonders, so that he maketh fire come down from heaven on the earth in the sight of men, and deceiveth them that dwell on the earth by the means of those miracles which he had power to do.” Revelation 13:13, 14. Men are deceived by miracles Satan’s agents actually perform, not merely pretend to do.

The very name of witchcraft is now held in contempt, and connections with evil spirits regarded as a fable of the Dark Ages. Yet Spiritualism, with millions of converts, has entered scientific circles, churches, legislative bodies, and even kings’ courts—this massive deception is merely a revival, in new disguise, of the witchcraft condemned of old.

Satan beguiles men now as he beguiled Eve, by exciting desire for forbidden knowledge: “Ye shall be as gods.” The wisdom Spiritualism imparts is earthly, sensual, devilish (James 3:15). With a masterly mind he adapts temptations to every class, working “with all deceivableness of unrighteousness.” He succeeds only as men voluntarily yield, indulging evil traits that lead to ruin and enable them to ruin others.

To the educated and refined he presents Spiritualism in intellectual forms, exciting imagination and pride until they despise the Eternal One. He appears as an angel of light, appealing to reason with elevating themes and enlisting affections with portrayals of love and charity. To the self-indulgent and sensual he offers grosser forms, leaving them free to follow the carnal heart. He tempts to excess even in lawful things, weakening body, mind, and morals, brutalizing human nature and sweeping multitudes who profess Christ into his net.

None need be deceived. The spirits make no difference between righteousness and sin, representing the basest men as exalted in Heaven, virtually declaring: No matter how wicked you are, Heaven is your home. They contradict what the apostles wrote under the Holy Spirit, deny the Bible’s divine origin, and tear away the Christian’s hope. Satan makes the world view Scripture as fiction and substitutes his own controlled manifestations, putting Christ in the background while exalting his own miracles.

Isaiah warns: “When they shall say unto you, Seek unto them that have familiar spirits… should not a people seek unto their God? … To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them.” Isaiah 8:19, 20. Had men received the truth that the dead know not anything, they would recognize Spiritualism as Satan’s working with power, signs, and lying wonders. But multitudes close their eyes to light, and “because they received not the love of the truth… God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie” (2 Thessalonians 2:10, 11).

Those opposing Spiritualism contend against Satan and his angels. They must meet him, as Christ did, with “It is written.” In the near future devils’ spirits will personate relatives and friends, declaring dangerous heresies and working miracles. We must withstand them with Bible truth: the dead know not anything, and these visitants are spirits of devils.

Just ahead is the “hour of temptation, which shall come upon all the world” (Revelation 3:10). All whose faith is not firmly founded on God’s word will be deceived. But to those who earnestly seek truth, God will be a sure defense and will sooner send every angel to protect His people than allow one trusting soul to be overcome.

Long has Satan prepared his final deception, founded on the lie to Eve: “Ye shall not surely die.” Spiritualism is his masterpiece, not yet fully accomplished but soon to sweep the world into fatal security, to be awakened only by God’s wrath. “Judgment also will I lay to the line and the hail shall sweep away the refuge of lies And your covenant with death shall be disannulled” (Isaiah 28:17, 18).
